## Introduction

In this notebook we do analysis for ICPhS paper on gesture-speech physics in counting-out rhymes

## Detailed explanation of the study and the type of data and variables

Eleven native speakers (three male) of Polish were asked to perform six counting-out rhymes in two different movement conditions and one still condition. The movement conditions involved the counting-out movement with the left or the right hand, and the still condition involved reading the rhyme without any movement. All speakers were right-handed. Additionally, in the movement conditions, speakers were asked to repeat the rhyme with enhanced speed, resulting in another condition. 

Altogether, these sum up to five conditions:

* left hand normal speed
* left hand fast speed
* right hand normal speed
* right hand fast speed
* reading

The order of the blocks was the same for all participants (reading, natural, fast), but the order of counting-out rhymes was randomized as well as whether they began with the dominant or non-dominant hand.

In all of those conditions, the participants performed six counting-out rhymes, the order of which was randomized across participants (cf. rhyme_order.xlsx or columns 6:11 in info.xlsx).

The participants were asked to perform each rhyme with a confederate teddy bear placed in front of them. For each condition, the participants were standing.

## Data wrangling

In this analysis, we are working only with wrist markers, as we expect the wrist coordinates to have more pronounced effects
```{r datasets for models, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning = FALSE}

### we filter the data in which peaks happen in pause, since this cannot be a real peak

kin_wrist <- subset(kin_wrist, env_syllable != '<p:>')

### Let's build the dataset we will use for statistic analysis
### We need to
 #1 filter out peaks that happens in acoustic-kinematic synchrony higher than 80 ms as we expect that only tight synchrony can lead to effects
 #2 filter out envelope amplitude peaks in which F0 is 0, as these cannot be real peaks
### We are building the datasets for each acoustic-kinematic pair

## env and acc in wrist with synchrony lower/higher than +-80
df_envacc_sync_w <- subset(kin_wrist, wrist_accenv_sync >= -80 & wrist_accenv_sync <= 80)
df_envacc_sync_w <- subset(df_envacc_sync_w, wrist_f0_accenvpeak != 0) ## put away envpeaks where f0 = 0
# you can save it
write.csv(df_envacc_sync_w, paste0(datasets, "dataset_env_acc.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## f0 and acc in wrist with synchrony lower/higher than +-80
df_f0acc_sync_w <- subset(kin_wrist, wrist_accf0_sync >= -80 & wrist_accf0_sync <= 80)
# you can save it
write.csv(df_f0acc_sync_w, paste0(datasets, "dataset_f0_acc.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# env and dec in wrist with synchrony lower/higher than +-80
df_envdec_sync_w <- subset(kin_wrist, wrist_decenv_sync >= -80 & wrist_decenv_sync <= 80)
df_envdec_sync_w <- subset(df_envdec_sync_w, wrist_f0_decenvpeak != 0)
# you can save it
write.csv(df_envdec_sync_w, paste0(datasets, "dataset_env_dec.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# f0 and dec in wrist with synchrony lower/higher than +-80
df_f0dec_sync_w <- subset(kin_wrist, wrist_decf0_sync >= -80 & wrist_decf0_sync <= 80)
# you can save it
write.csv(df_f0dec_sync_w, paste0(datasets, "dataset_f0_dec.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## Note that we do not filter out outliers before saving datasets for statistical analysis. They are removed in script with statistical analysis
```

## Data wrangling and annotation

We detect outliers using function outlierKD that removes them by Tukey rules on quartiles +/- 1.5 IQR. This code should be run in the console, because the function prompts the user to answer whether they wish to remove the outliers or not.

```{r outliers and synchrony annotation, include=FALSE, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning = FALSE}

#Function
#source("http://goo.gl/UUyEzD")
# in the form of outlierKD(f0_dec, wrist_f0peak_dec)
outlierKD <- function(dt, var) {
     var_name <- eval(substitute(var),eval(dt))
     na1 <- sum(is.na(var_name))
     m1 <- mean(var_name, na.rm = T)
     par(mfrow=c(2, 2), oma=c(0,0,3,0))
     boxplot(var_name, main="With outliers")
     hist(var_name, main="With outliers", xlab=NA, ylab=NA)
     outlier <- boxplot.stats(var_name)$out
     mo <- mean(outlier)
     var_name <- ifelse(var_name %in% outlier, NA, var_name)
     boxplot(var_name, main="Without outliers")
     hist(var_name, main="Without outliers", xlab=NA, ylab=NA)
     title("Outlier Check", outer=TRUE)
     na2 <- sum(is.na(var_name))
     cat("Outliers identified:", na2 - na1, "n")
     cat("Propotion (%) of outliers:", round((na2 - na1) / sum(!is.na(var_name))*100, 1), "n")
     cat("Mean of the outliers:", round(mo, 2), "n")
     m2 <- mean(var_name, na.rm = T)
     cat("Mean without removing outliers:", round(m1, 2), "n")
     cat("Mean if we remove outliers:", round(m2, 2), "n")
     response <- readline(prompt="Do you want to remove outliers and to replace with NA? [yes/no]: ")
     if(response == "y" | response == "yes"){
          dt[as.character(substitute(var))] <- invisible(var_name)
          assign(as.character(as.list(match.call())$dt), dt, envir = .GlobalEnv)
          cat("Outliers successfully removed", "n")
          return(invisible(dt))
     } else{
          cat("Nothing changed", "n")
          return(invisible(var_name))
     }
}
```

We also want to annotate the dataset with synchrony information.
```{r synchrony information, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning = FALSE}

### if sync value is negative - kinematic peak leads the acoustic peak
### if sync value is positive - kinematic peak follows the acoustic peak
### if the sync value is between -25 and +25 - acoustic and kinematic peaks are closely synced

## ENV-ACC
df_envacc_sync_w$peak_sync <- NA
df_envacc_sync_w$peak_sync <- ifelse(df_envacc_sync_w$wrist_accenv_sync < -25, 'kpeak leads', ifelse(df_envacc_sync_w$wrist_accenv_sync >= -25 & df_envacc_sync_w$wrist_accenv_sync <= 25, 'closely synced', 'kpeak follows'))

## F0-ACC
df_f0acc_sync_w$peak_sync <- NA
df_f0acc_sync_w$peak_sync <- ifelse(df_f0acc_sync_w$wrist_accf0_sync < -25, 'kpeak leads', ifelse(df_f0acc_sync_w$wrist_accf0_sync >= -25 & df_f0acc_sync_w$wrist_accf0_sync <= 25, 'closely synced', 'kpeak follows'))

## ENV-DEC
df_envdec_sync_w$peak_sync <- NA
df_envdec_sync_w$peak_sync <- ifelse(df_envdec_sync_w$wrist_decenv_sync < -25, 'kpeak leads', ifelse(df_envdec_sync_w$wrist_decenv_sync >= -25 & df_envdec_sync_w$wrist_decenv_sync <= 25, 'closely synced', 'kpeak follows'))

## F0-DEC
df_f0dec_sync_w$peak_sync <- NA
df_f0dec_sync_w$peak_sync <- ifelse(df_f0dec_sync_w$wrist_decf0_sync < -25, 'kpeak leads', ifelse(df_f0dec_sync_w$wrist_decf0_sync >= -25 & df_f0dec_sync_w$wrist_decf0_sync <= 25, 'closely synced', 'kpeak follows'))

```

Acceleration-envelope
```{r wrist acc-env plot, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning = FALSE}

# let's get a normalized amplitude envelope values
df_envacc_sync_w$wrist_envpeak_acc_norm <- NA
df_envacc_sync_w$wrist_envpeak_acc_norm <- ave(df_envacc_sync_w$wrist_envpeak_acc, df_envacc_sync_w$speaker, FUN = function(x) scale(x, center = FALSE, scale = TRUE))

# this is a basic plot exploring relationship between acceleration and amplitude envelope
# note that we multiply acceleration by *100*200 to get to cm/s^2
```

2. Kinematic peak: deceleration

Deceleration-envelope - **This plot we used in the paper**
```{r wrist dec-env plot, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning = FALSE}

# let's get a normalized amplitude envelope values
df_envdec_sync_w$wrist_envpeak_dec_norm <- NA
df_envdec_sync_w$wrist_envpeak_dec_norm <- ave(df_envdec_sync_w$wrist_envpeak_dec, df_envdec_sync_w$speaker, FUN = function(x) scale(x, center = FALSE, scale = TRUE))

## for esthetic reasons, we want to get rid of the underscore
df_envdec_sync_w$point_direct <- ifelse(df_envdec_sync_w$point_direct == 'backward_movement', 'backward movement', 'forward movement')

# this is a basic plot exploring relationship between deceleration and envelope
# note that we multiply acceleration by *100*200 to get to cm/s^2
# we use both lm and loess for capturing possible non-linearity

plot_decenv_w <- ggplot(df_envdec_sync_w, aes(x = wrist_decpeak*100*200, y = wrist_envpeak_dec_norm))+
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5, color = 'black')+
  geom_smooth(method=loess, color = 'black', linetype = 'dashed', linewidth = 0.4, fill = 'gray', alpha = 0.5)+
  geom_smooth(method=lm, color = 'red', linewidth = 2, fill = 'red')+
  labs(x = "Deceleration peak, wrist (cm/s^2)", y = "Amplitude envelope peak (normalized)")+
  theme_cowplot(12)+
  scale_x_reverse(labels = abs)+
  ylim(0.25,1.5)+
  theme(title = element_text(size = 10), text = element_text(family = "times"))

# distinguishing by different feature

plot_decenv_w_all <- plot_decenv_w + facet_wrap(~sp_rate*speaker, ncol=11) # per trial
plot_decenv_w_speaker <- plot_decenv_w + facet_wrap(~speaker, ncol=6) # per speaker
plot_decenv_w_rhyme <- plot_decenv_w + facet_wrap(~rhyme, ncol=6) # per rhyme
plot_decenv_w_rate <- plot_decenv_w + facet_wrap(~sp_rate, ncol=2) # per speech rate



### this plot we use in paper
plot_decenv_w_dir <- plot_decenv_w + facet_wrap(~point_direct, ncol=2) # per movement direction

## save it
ggsave(file.path(plots, "decenv_plot.png"), dpi = 300)
ggsave(file.path(plots, "decenv_plot.jpg"), dpi = 300)


```

This chunk creates plot with example of amplitude envelope, F0 and acceleration time series (first 3.4 seconds from the onset of speech).
There are two plots with acceleration and 1) amplitude envelope, and 2) F0. There are also two smaller zoomed plots that introduce the peaks under study. 
```{r time series plot, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning = FALSE}

beauty_colors <- brewer.pal(6, 'Set1') #produce 6 nice diverging colors

######### F0 - ACCELERATION

#let's not have 0 values in the plot, just have gaps of none-voicing
sam$f0 <- ifelse(sam$f0==0, NA, sam$f0)

# let's change unit of acceleration to cm/s^2
sam$a_wrist <- sam$a_wrist*100*200

#for setting the correct ranges to be used as a second axes
  # https://stackoverflow.com/questions/3099219/ggplot-with-2-y-axes-on-each-side-and-different-scales
ylim.f <- range(sam$f0[!is.na(sam$f0)])
ylim.a <- range(sam$a_wrist)  

b <- diff(ylim.f)/diff(ylim.a ) #scaling  factor b of the differences in ranges
a <- ylim.f[1] - b*ylim.a[1]

# plotting

f0acc <- ggplot(sam, aes(x = time_ms)) +
  geom_path(aes(y = f0), color = beauty_colors[1], linewidth = 1) +
  geom_path(aes(y = a+a_wrist*b), color = beauty_colors[2], linewidth = 1.) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = 4100, xmax = 4450, ymin = 150, ymax = 400), color = 'black', linetype='dashed', alpha = 0)+ # for dashed-lined area that is zoomed in next plot
  theme_cowplot(12)+ scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1")+ theme(
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(color = beauty_colors[1]),
    axis.text.y.left = element_text(color = beauty_colors[1]),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = beauty_colors[2]),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(color = beauty_colors[2]))+
  scale_y_continuous(
    "F0 (Hz)", 
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ (. - a)/b, name = "acceleration (cm/s^2)")
  )+ labs(x = '')+
  xlim(2543,6000)+
  theme(title = element_text(size = 10), text = element_text(family = "times"))


####### ENVELOPE - ACCELERATION

#for setting the correct ranges to be used as a second axes
ylim.env <- range(sam$env)
ylim.acc <- range(sam$a_wrist)  

bb <- diff(ylim.env)/diff(ylim.acc ) #scaling  factor b of the differences in ranges
aa <- ylim.env[1] - bb*ylim.acc[1]

## plotting 

envacc <- ggplot(sam, aes(x = time_ms)) +
  geom_path(aes(y = env), color = beauty_colors[3], linewidth = 1) +
  geom_path(aes(y = aa+a_wrist*bb), color = beauty_colors[2], linewidth = 1.) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = 4100, xmax = 4450, ymin = 0, ymax = 0.15), color = 'black', linetype='dashed', alpha = 0)+ # for dashed-lined area that is zoomed in next plot
  theme_cowplot(12)+ scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1")+ theme(
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(color = beauty_colors[3]),
    axis.text.y.left = element_text(color = beauty_colors[3]),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = beauty_colors[2]),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(color = beauty_colors[2]))+
  scale_y_continuous(
    "amplitude envelope", 
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ (. - aa)/bb, name = "acceleration (cm/s^2)")
  ) + xlab('time (ms)')+
  xlim(2543,6000)+
  theme(title = element_text(size = 10), text = element_text(family = "times"))

  geom_vline(xintercept = wdec_peaks_time, color = beauty_colors[4], linetype = 'solid', linewidth = 1)+
  geom_vline(xintercept = wenv_peaks_time, color = beauty_colors[3], linetype = 'solid', linewidth = 1)+
  geom_point(data = sam_peaks, aes(x = wrist_apeak_time , y = aa+wrist_apeak*bb*100*200), color = beauty_colors[2], size = 5) +
  geom_text(data = sam_peaks, aes(x = wrist_apeak_time, y = aa+wrist_apeak*bb*100*200, label = 'A'))+
  geom_point(data = sam_peaks, aes(x = wrist_decpeak_time, y = aa+wrist_decpeak*bb*100*200), color = beauty_colors[4], size = 5) +
  geom_text(data = sam_peaks, aes(x = wrist_decpeak_time, y =  aa+wrist_decpeak*bb*100*200, label = 'B'))+
  geom_point(data = sam_peaks, aes(x = wrist_envpeak_acc_time , y = wrist_envpeak_acc), color = beauty_colors[3], size = 5) +
  geom_text(data = sam_peaks, aes(x = wrist_envpeak_acc_time, y = wrist_envpeak_acc, label = 'D'))+
  theme_cowplot(12)+ scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1")+ theme(
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(color = beauty_colors[3]),
    axis.text.y.left = element_text(color = beauty_colors[3]),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = beauty_colors[2]),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(color = beauty_colors[2]))+
  scale_y_continuous(
    "", 
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ (. - aa)/bb, name = "")
  ) + xlab('')+
  xlim(4100,4450)

## get rid of descriptions
envacc_z <- envacc_zoom + 
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y.left = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y.left = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y.left = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y.right = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y.right = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y.right = element_blank()
  )


## Now let's put it together

# Arrange the plots in a grid with two rows and two columns
timeseries <- grid.arrange(f0acc, f0acc_z, envacc, envacc_z, 
             widths = c(0.7, 1/3))

# save it 
ggsave(file.path(plots, "timeseries.eps"), plot = timeseries, device = "eps")
```
